title: Tech Note: Using LDAP with 4D part II
author: Pierre Bonnais

historical_commentary.text: This note captures a very real, era-specific pain point: porting native C/C++ 4D plug-ins from the classic Mac OS resource-fork/CFM world to Mac OS X's then-new Mach-O runtime, including obscure linker fixes like the dyld_stub_bindin_helper/bundle1.o issue. That porting problem itself is now purely of historical interest since 4D plug-in development has moved on from CodeWarrior-era Mach-O bundle mechanics entirely. LDAP as a directory protocol, however, remains genuinely still relevant today (e.g., via Active Directory), though modern 4D applications more often authenticate through SSO/OAuth identity providers or later, higher-level LDAP libraries rather than a custom Mach-O plug-in and On Web Authentication bind as shown here.
related_updates: 4D plug-in development has long since moved past the CodeWarrior/Mach-O-bundle porting mechanics described in this note
LDAP directory services remain in wide enterprise use today, though many modern web applications now favor SSO/OAuth-based identity providers over direct LDAP binds in On Web Authentication
